text:
sam: Heads-up — new quantized-ranker CANARY (v2-int8) shows a ~3.5% MRR drop vs float on the medical cohort (cohort=bmed-2025). NDCG looks stable but top1 is down, concentrated on short queries (<6 tokens). Anyone free to glance?

maya: Oof. Can you paste the canary benchmark table or a quick csv?

sam: quick summary + link to raw: s3://redwood-bench/rerank/canary/1719994322/summary.csv
```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1
float32,bmed-2025,0.634,0.498,0.52
int8,bmed-2025,0.631,0.481,0.45
float32,web-std,0.612,0.502,0.53
int8,web-std,0.611,0.500,0.52
```

lee: That top1 delta on bmed short queries is suspicious. Two quick suspects: tokenizer differences (unicode + punctuation) or candidate pool normalization/order change in preproc. Did the canary use the exact same candidate generation + ordering pipeline?

sam: Candidate generation was same job id, ordering is deterministic in the harness. I dug a bit — there is a tiny tokenizer mapping diff from the opt-quant patch (remapped some rare unicode like 'α' and some punctuation clusters). Running tokenizer-parity across the cohort now.

anika: Also remember we pushed a scaling tweak to the int8 codepath last month that alters final logits rescaling slightly. Could be softmax temp/norm interacting.

morgan: +1 on checking final-layer scaling. Also do a per-query dump where float vs int8 disagree (top-k texts) — that helps see if it's semantic flip or just score jitter.

sam: Uploaded 10 example disagreement cases to the bucket and pasted one small example below where float ranks doc_A > doc_B but int8 flips (texts redacted):
```
query: "pediatric hypertension guidelines"
float_top2: [doc_A (clinical-review), doc_B (case-series)]
int8_top2:  [doc_B, doc_A]
notes: doc_A has greek alpha char in title, tokenized differently in int8 run
```

ci-bot: Perf job 1719994400 finished — logs at https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/1719994400

maya: Can we do an ablation: int8 but with float32 copy of the final linear layer (mixed last-layer) to isolate whether last-layer quantization is source? If that recovers MRR, action is clear.

sam: Queued mixed-last-layer run on dedicated GPU, ETA ~30m. Also running full tokenizer parity diff across bmed-2025 to correlate token diffs with top1 flips.

lee: If tokenizer diffs correlate strongly with flips, we should canonicalize medical unicode and punctuation before tokenization for the medical cohort (pre-token normalize step).

anika: Also add an eval slice for query_len<6 to the canary dashboards — we keep missing these micro-slices in rollouts.

morgan: Creating a short GT ticket and adding to the reranker-onboard checklist: [tokenizer parity check, mixed-last-layer ablation, per-query disagreement dump]. I'll link ticket soon.

sam: Thanks — will post mixed-run results and parity diff once ready. ping me if you want early access to the dump. :thumbsup:
